1	# Configuration reference
2	
3	`.agent-context/config.yaml` is canonical, reviewed project data. The copied
4	`.agent-context/config.schema.json` is generated editor support and is repaired by `carrylog sync`.
5	
6	## Version contract
7	
8	Configuration versions `1` and `2` are supported. Configuration version and npm package version are
9	separate; unknown versions and cross-version adapter names fail before any write.
10	
11	Version 1 is the frozen published compatibility contract. Version 2 adds universal agent surfaces and
12	continuity policy. New initialization creates v2, while existing v1 repositories remain valid and are
13	never rewritten implicitly. See [ADR-0005](decisions/0005-configuration-v1-compatibility.md) and
14	[ADR-0009](decisions/0009-configuration-v2-and-universal-surfaces.md).
15	
16	Every runtime-decoder-accepted configuration also passes its versioned public JSON Schema. JSON
17	Schema validation alone is insufficient: runtime checks additionally enforce normalized ownership,
18	checkpoint references, portable paths, symlink rejection, actual content budgets, and filesystem
19	state.
20	
21	The recommended first line enables YAML editor validation:
22	
23	```yaml
24	# yaml-language-server: $schema=./config.schema.json
25	```
26	
27	An older v1 file without this comment remains valid at runtime. `validate` emits
28	`W_CONFIG_SCHEMA_HEADER`; add the comment manually after review. `sync` does not rewrite canonical
29	YAML.
30	
31	## Fields
32	
33	### `version`
34	
35	Required integer. Must be `1` or `2`.
36	
37	### `project.name`
38	
39	Required single-line string, 1–120 Unicode characters. Leading/trailing whitespace and reserved
40	managed-marker text are rejected.
41	
42	### `documents`
43	
44	Required array with 1–256 entries and at least one `load: always` entry.
45	
46	| Field | Contract |
47	| --- | --- |
48	| `id` | Unique lowercase identifier matching `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, at most 64 characters |
49	| `path` | Unique path relative to `.agent-context/`, at most 1024 Unicode characters |
50	| `load` | `always` or `on-demand` |
51	| `description` | Single-line router description, at most 240 characters |
52	| `triggers` | Optional non-empty list of at most 32 single-line strings, each at most 120 characters |
53	
54	Document path uniqueness uses conservative Unicode compatibility and multi-step case normalization
55	for cross-platform safety. This can intentionally reject names that coexist on one filesystem when
56	another supported filesystem may alias them.
57	
58	Version 1 uses document ID `handoff` for `carrylog handoff`. Version 2 uses
59	`continuity.checkpointDocument`, whose target must exist and use `load: always`.
60	
61	The complete instructions template published in `@jaemani/agent-context-kit@0.1.0-beta.3` defines
62	the old-package-to-Carrylog migration boundary independently of a mutable document ID or path.
63	Carrylog can replace that exact template while
64	preserving LF or CRLF line endings. Customized always-loaded context with a command-shaped invocation
65	of the removed `ackit` executable is invalid until a maintainer reviews and changes the command;
66	historical prose and other human content are not inferred from a template.
67	
68	### `adapters`
69	
70	Required array with 1–32 entries.
71	
72	| Field | Contract |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| `type` | v1: `codex` or `claude`; v2: `agents`, `claude`, or `gemini` |
75	| `output` | Unique project-relative instruction-file path |
76	
77	The v2 `agents` surface is shared by Codex and Cursor and defaults to `AGENTS.md`; this avoids two
78	logical harnesses competing for one output. `claude` defaults to `CLAUDE.md`, and `gemini` defaults to
79	`GEMINI.md`.
80	
81	### `continuity` (v2 only)
82	
83	| Field | Contract |
84	| --- | --- |
85	| `checkpointDocument` | ID of one configured `load: always` document |
86	| `generateSkills` | Generate and validate the shared `.agents` Skill and Claude adapter Skill |
87	
88	When Skill generation is disabled, existing Carrylog-marked Skills are not deleted automatically;
89	`validate` warns so their removal remains an explicit reviewed action.
90	
91	The generated continuity Skill resolves executables offline in a fixed order: a compatible Carrylog
92	source build, the nearest compatible project-pinned package, then a compatible global installation.
93	Each selected candidate must support `resume`; an incompatible pinned candidate stops with explicit
94	guidance instead of falling through or downloading another version.
95	
96	Every config, document, copied schema, and adapter output has exclusive path ownership. Exact,
97	case-folded, or Unicode-normalized collisions fail before planning writes.
98	
99	### `policies`
100	
101	- `maxAlwaysCharacters`: total JavaScript character units allowed across `always` documents;
102	- `maxAdapterCharacters`: maximum generated managed block per adapter.
103	
104	Both are required integers from 1,000 through 100,000. These deterministic budgets are not claims
105	about a particular model tokenizer. Independently of those configurable rendering budgets, portable
106	resume observes at most 8 MiB across the configuration and all canonical documents in one pass. This
107	fixed aggregate read limit prevents a large on-demand catalog from multiplying per-file limits into
108	unbounded retained memory.
109	
110	## Portable path rules
111	
112	Paths use `/`, remain relative and normalized, and cannot contain `.`/`..` segments, empty segments,
113	NUL/control characters, Windows-reserved names/characters, trailing dots/spaces, or reserved marker
114	text. Existing symlink components are rejected. A valid-looking schema path can still fail runtime
115	ownership or filesystem checks.
116	
117	## Explicit v1 migration
118	
119	```bash
120	carrylog migrate --to 2 --universal --dry-run
121	carrylog migrate --to 2 --universal
122	carrylog validate
123	```
124	
125	Without `--universal`, migration preserves the selected v1 surfaces and leaves Skill generation
126	disabled. With it, Carrylog ensures `agents`, `claude`, and `gemini` surfaces and enables Skills. A
127	stock v1 handoff can be converted automatically; customized prose must already satisfy the checkpoint
128	section contract or migration stops with `E_CHECKPOINT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`.
129	
130	Migration preserves YAML comments and LF/CRLF style, preflights all outputs, and writes config last.
131	`--check` exits 1 when migration work remains; `--dry-run` prints the plan without writing.
132	
133	`sync`, `validate`, `handoff`, `checkpoint`, `migrate`, and `resume` discover the nearest
134	`.agent-context/config.yaml` while walking upward from the explicit or current root. They can
135	therefore run from a nested project directory. `init` treats its explicit or current root as the new
136	project root and does not perform upward discovery.
137	
138	## Version 2 example
139	
140	```yaml
141	# yaml-language-server: $schema=./config.schema.json
142	version: 2
143	project:
144	  name: Example service
145	documents:
146	  - id: handoff
147	    path: handoff.md
148	    load: always
149	    description: Verified portable checkpoint and next action
150	  - id: architecture
151	    path: architecture.md
152	    load: on-demand
153	    description: System boundaries and module responsibilities
154	    triggers:
155	      - architecture changes
156	adapters:
157	  - type: agents
158	    output: AGENTS.md
159	  - type: claude
160	    output: CLAUDE.md
161	  - type: gemini
162	    output: GEMINI.md
163	continuity:
164	  checkpointDocument: handoff
165	  generateSkills: true
166	policies:
167	  maxAlwaysCharacters: 16000
168	  maxAdapterCharacters: 12000
169	```
170

1	# ADR-0005: Freeze configuration v1 and separate structural from semantic validation
2	
3	- Status: Accepted
4	- Date: 2026-07-10
5	- Owners: Repository maintainer
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	The alpha decoder already called its configuration `version: 1`, but no public schema or compatibility
10	promise defined what that version meant. Editor validation, runtime validation, and future package
11	upgrades could therefore disagree or silently reinterpret an existing repository.
12	
13	JSON Schema can describe object shape, bounds, enumerations, and many string constraints. It cannot
14	reliably express every cross-entry invariant used here, including Unicode/case-normalized path
15	collisions, adapter-to-source ownership, symbolic links, and actual filesystem budgets.
16	
17	## Decision
18	
19	Package SemVer and configuration versions are independent:
20	
21	- npm package versions describe CLI/API releases;
22	- the integer `version` in `config.yaml` describes the canonical data contract.
23	
24	Configuration v1 is the first beta contract. Every raw configuration accepted by the v1 runtime
25	decoder must also pass `schemas/config-v1.schema.json`. The reverse is intentionally not guaranteed:
26	runtime validation adds documented semantic and filesystem rules that JSON Schema cannot express.
27	Strings are not silently trimmed; surrounding whitespace is invalid.
28	
29	The v1 schema has a stable `$id`, is shipped in the npm package, and is copied into each initialized
30	repository. `sync` repairs a missing or drifted copied schema but does not rewrite canonical YAML.
31	A pre-schema v1 project remains runnable; `validate` warns when the editor directive is missing and
32	documents the exact manual addition.
33	
34	Unknown configuration versions fail before mutation. There is no migration command while v1 is the
35	only version. A future v2 must ship an explicit, reviewable migration workflow with check/dry-run
36	behavior before any command rewrites v1 data. Support for v1 will not be removed within package 0.x
37	or 1.x. Removing it later requires a package major release and a documented migration path.
38	
39	After the first beta tag, changes that make a previously accepted safe v1 configuration invalid are
40	breaking changes. A demonstrated security defect may require a narrower rejection, but it must be
41	documented in the changelog and covered by a regression test.
42	
43	## Rejected alternatives
44	
45	- **Treat the schema as the complete validator:** rejected because filesystem and normalized
46	  ownership rules cannot be represented accurately.
47	- **Silently normalize whitespace or paths:** rejected because the rendered value would differ from
48	  reviewed YAML.
49	- **Let the installed CLI reinterpret v1 over time:** rejected because repositories could change
50	  behavior without changing their canonical version.
51	- **Add a no-op migration command now:** rejected because it would create an interface without a
52	  real source/target transformation to validate.
53	
54	## Consequences
55	
56	- Schema/runtime parity needs a permanent generated and boundary corpus.
57	- New configuration concepts that cannot be added compatibly require v2.
58	- The copied schema is generated ownership and must participate in the same collision graph as every
59	  document and adapter.
60	- Older alpha repositories may receive a non-blocking editor-directive warning after upgrading.
61	
62	## Validation
63	
64	- Strict Ajv compilation and boundary tests for the public schema.
65	- A deterministic 500-case corpus proving runtime-accepted generated v1 configs pass the schema.
66	- Upgrade coverage for missing schema artifacts and missing YAML directives.
67	- Exact package and initialized-project schema byte comparisons.
68

1	# ADR-0009: Add explicit configuration v2 for universal agent surfaces
2	
3	- Status: Accepted
4	- Date: 2026-07-11
5	- Owners: Repository maintainer
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Configuration v1 is a published compatibility contract. It names Codex and Claude Code adapters
10	directly and has no continuity policy. Adding Cursor, Gemini CLI, generated Skills, or checkpoint
11	selection by silently changing v1 would make the same reviewed YAML mean something different after a
12	package upgrade.
13	
14	Codex and Cursor use the same repository instruction surface, while Claude Code and Gemini CLI use
15	distinct root files. Treating every harness as a separate adapter would duplicate `AGENTS.md`
16	ownership and create invalid output collisions.
17	
18	## Decision
19	
20	Carrylog supports configuration versions 1 and 2 concurrently. New `init` operations create v2;
21	existing v1 repositories remain valid and are never migrated by `sync`.
22	
23	Version 2 adds:
24	
25	- adapter surfaces `agents`, `claude`, and `gemini` rather than one entry per harness;
26	- `agents` as the shared `AGENTS.md` surface for Codex and Cursor;
27	- `continuity.checkpointDocument`, which must identify an always-loaded document;
28	- `continuity.generateSkills`, which controls deterministic repository Skill generation.
29	
30	Each version has a separate packaged JSON Schema and copied `.agent-context/config.schema.json`.
31	Runtime decoding rejects cross-version adapter names. Configuration v1 schema bytes, `$id`, marker
32	namespaces, and semantics remain frozen under ADR-0005 and ADR-0008.
33	
34	`carrylog migrate --to 2` is the only v1-to-v2 transition. It preserves YAML comments and LF/CRLF
35	style, maps `codex` to `agents`, and adds continuity policy. `--universal` ensures all three surfaces
36	and enables Skills; it can also complete a partial v2 configuration. A stock published v1 handoff is
37	converted automatically, and an already compliant checkpoint is preserved. Customized handoff prose
38	without the required checkpoint sections fails with `E_CHECKPOINT_REVIEW_REQUIRED` rather than being
39	semantically reclassified.
40	
41	Migration plans schema, adapter, Skill, checkpoint, and config changes before mutation. Unowned
42	adapter files still require `--adopt`; Skills are never adopted or merged. The config rename is last
43	in the guarded batch so a process failure cannot leave v2 claiming outputs that were not attempted.
44	This ordering narrows failure impact but does not claim an OS-level cross-file transaction.
45	
46	## Rejected alternatives
47	
48	- **Extend v1 in place:** rejected because it violates the published meaning of v1.
49	- **One adapter per harness:** rejected because Codex and Cursor would compete for `AGENTS.md`.
50	- **Implicit migration during `sync`:** rejected because customized handoff semantics require review.
51	- **Infer customized checkpoint sections with a model:** rejected because migration must remain
52	  deterministic, offline, and auditable.
53	- **Drop v1 after introducing v2:** rejected by the compatibility period in ADR-0005.
54	
55	## Consequences
56	
57	- Code paths and tests must keep version-specific adapter and schema contracts distinct.
58	- A user who wants all supported harnesses runs `migrate --to 2 --universal`; a narrower migration
59	  preserves the surfaces they selected.
60	- New harnesses should map to an existing discovery surface when ownership is truly shared, otherwise
61	  a future configuration version may be required.
62	- Generated Skill paths participate in normalized managed-path ownership only while Skills are
63	  enabled; disabling generation leaves existing managed Skills for explicit human removal and warns.
64	
65	## Validation
66	
67	- Strict schema/runtime tests for both versions and 500 generated valid v2 configurations.
68	- Partial v1 and v2 universal migrations, non-universal migration, idempotence, comment and CRLF
69	  preservation, output collisions, customized checkpoints, and unowned Skill conflicts.
70	- No-partial-write assertions for every planning conflict and config-last ordering review.
71	- Carrylog's own repository migration from v1 to universal v2 followed by clean sync and validation.
72

1	# ADR-0012: Require evidence gates before expanding continuity claims
2	
3	- Status: Accepted
4	- Date: 2026-07-12
5	- Owners: Repository maintainer
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	ADR-0010 deliberately limits Carrylog continuity to reviewed repository state plus fresh Git
10	evidence. Later discussion considered visible delivery receipts, observable session journals,
11	cross-harness launch wrappers, and reversible compaction. Those ideas could improve the experience,
12	but the project has not demonstrated that arbitrary harness switching preserves effective context,
13	that retaining all observable conversation improves outcomes, or that Carrylog compaction would
14	outperform harness-native resume or compaction.
15	
16	The initial audit brief proposed a comprehensive factorial evaluation. External review agreed with
17	its evidence discipline but found the first execution plan too large for a solo beta. Waiting for a
18	full research program would leave the project in a permanent pre-release state; implementing the
19	features first would turn unproven assumptions into product contracts.
20	
21	## Decision
22	
23	Carrylog retains the accepted ADR-0010 boundary. It is a repository-owned project-memory governance
24	and checkpoint tool, not a conversation-replay product.
25	
26	Continuity evidence is classified in increasing strength:
27	
28	1. **artifact:** the expected repository state exists and is current;
29	2. **delivery:** the intended state is demonstrably included in model-visible input;
30	3. **reconstruction:** the model recovers preregistered relevant facts and constraints;
31	4. **behavior:** the next task preserves decisions, avoids repeated work, and uses prior state;
32	5. **perception:** the user correctly understands what continued and experiences useful continuity.
33	
34	Evidence at one level does not prove the next. A generated file, discovery trace, receipt, or model
35	acknowledgement is not behavioral continuity.
36	
37	Before session journaling or semantic compaction becomes a supported runtime feature or enabled
38	default, the project must run a minimum viable Tier 1 pilot:
39	
40	- two materially different repositories;
41	- five continuation tasks per repository;
42	- no-context, manual-handoff, and current Carrylog checkpoint conditions;
43	- two authenticated harnesses;
44	- prompts, facts, prohibited reversals, rubrics, and analysis rules committed before execution;
45	- sanitized raw results and all exclusions retained for review.
46	
47	Tier 1 is an exploratory maintainer-run pilot, not external proof. It estimates variance, exposes
48	harness problems, and decides whether larger work is justified. An independent Tier 2 evaluation is
49	required before broad behavioral or compaction superiority claims.
50	
51	Research may prototype the minimum capture or delivery mechanism required to measure a hypothesis,
52	but prototypes stay outside the stable runtime contract. Carrylog must not default to automatic
53	semantic compaction, indefinite conversation retention, or raw transcript export before the
54	applicable evidence and privacy gates pass.
55	
56	Native resume and native compact are baselines, not obstacles to replace. If a harness exposes a
57	native compact artifact, an experiment may reuse it with provenance. An inaccessible native compact
58	cannot be described as portable or reconstructed. Carrylog compact, selected raw history, retrieval,
59	and hybrid approaches must be compared on factual retention, contradictions, task outcome, working
60	context, cost, latency, and exposure—not token reduction alone.
61	
62	Future session UX must distinguish at least `resume`, `branch`, `project-only`, and `fresh` intent.
63	Repository instruction discovery may still occur during a fresh conversation, so the product must
64	not equate fresh conversation with absence of project policy.
65	
66	The narrow checkpoint/resume beta is not blocked on proving every future continuity hypothesis. A
67	known research gap is documented and the beta may ship when its current claims, package, security,
68	review, and release gates pass. High-severity integrity or data-loss findings remain release blockers;
69	evidence work is not a reason to ignore them.
70	
71	Every new continuity feature must trace to a job in `docs/product-scope.md`. “More sophisticated” or
72	“more defensive” is not independently a product job.
73	
74	## Considered alternatives
75	
76	### Implement journaling and compaction before measurement
77	
78	Rejected. It would create retention, privacy, and compatibility contracts before demonstrating user
79	value.
80	
81	### Require the complete factorial audit before beta publication
82	
83	Rejected. The cost is disproportionate to the current narrow product claim and would prevent the
84	project from obtaining the users needed for meaningful evidence.
85	
86	### Treat a continuity receipt as proof
87	
88	Rejected. A receipt can attest attempted delivery and model acknowledgement but not correct use.
89	
90	### Reuse every harness-native compact automatically
91	
92	Rejected. Availability, format, hidden dependencies, and cross-harness value differ and require
93	per-harness evidence.
94	
95	### Market Carrylog as universal conversation resume
96	
97	Rejected until behavioral and perceived-continuity evidence supports that claim. The defensible
98	current position is Git-reviewable, tool-neutral project memory and checkpoint governance.
99	
100	## Consequences
101	
102	Positive:
103	
104	- the current beta can ship without pretending a research roadmap is already proven;
105	- small public experiments replace indefinite audit planning;
106	- receipts, journals, and compaction receive claim-specific gates;
107	- native harness behavior remains a measured baseline;
108	- future session designs must preserve explicit fresh and branch choices.
109	
110	Negative:
111	
112	- Carrylog cannot yet promise conversation continuity or arbitrary switch invariance;
113	- authenticated harness access and experimental execution are required before expansion;
114	- research artifacts need privacy review and may reveal that proposed features are not worthwhile;
115	- model and harness updates can expire earlier results.
116	
117	## Validation and evidence expiration
118	
119	- Execute the committed Tier 1 protocol under `research/continuity/` before promoting research
120	  journaling or compaction into the supported runtime.
121	- Report unavailable delivery evidence as unknown, not successful.
122	- Preserve model, harness, context-limit, prompt, repository, and commit identities with results.
123	- Re-run affected evidence when an instruction-discovery surface, model generation, native compact
124	  policy, or wrapper delivery path materially changes.
125	- Revisit this ADR if Tier 1 shows no useful signal, external users identify a different primary job,
126	  or a broadly adopted standard provides stronger portable continuity primitives.
127

1	# Carrylog
2	
3	One Git-reviewable project checkpoint for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI.
4	
5	Carrylog lets the repository—not one model session—own the current objective, decisions, risks,
6	verification, and next action. Initialize once, work with any supported agent, checkpoint the result,
7	and give the next agent one verified project-state envelope instead of another independently
8	maintained memory file.
9	
10	```text
11	Before: switch agent -> find and rewrite project state in another tool-specific file
12	After:  switch agent -> carrylog resume -> inspect one objective, evidence set, risk list, and next action
13	```
14	
15	Carrylog resumes project state, not a provider's private chat or hidden model state.
16	
17	> **Status:** `carrylog@0.1.0-beta.5` is published and independently verified on npm's explicit
18	> `beta` channel. First publication forced `latest` to remain at beta.4 until stable, so prerelease
19	> users should keep using `carrylog@beta` or an exact version. Current limits are
20	> tracked in [Current state](.agent-context/current-state.md) and
21	> [ADR-0010](docs/decisions/0010-portable-checkpoint-and-resume-boundary.md).
22	
23	## See the handoff
24	
25	```console
26	$ carrylog resume
27	Project: Example project
28	Objective: Replace the mock profile endpoint without changing the reviewed schema.
29	Next action: Implement the endpoint and run the package contract tests.
30	Checkpoint: ready
31	```
32	
33	The machine-readable form also includes checkpoint sections, content digests, a progressive context
34	catalog, and bounded Git evidence:
35	
36	```bash
37	carrylog resume --check --json
38	```
39	
40	Abbreviated output from the current contract:
41	
42	```json
43	{
44	  "formatVersion": 1,
45	  "project": {
46	    "name": "Example project",
47	    "configVersion": 2,
48	    "configPath": ".agent-context/config.yaml",
49	    "configSha256": "..."
50	  },
51	  "checkpoint": {
52	    "document": ".agent-context/handoff.md",
53	    "sha256": "...",
54	    "stale": false,
55	    "sections": {
56	      "Objective": "Replace the mock profile endpoint.",
57	      "Next action": "Implement the endpoint and run contract tests."
58	    }
59	  },
60	  "git": {
61	    "branch": "main",
62	    "staged": 0,
63	    "unstaged": 0,
64	    "untracked": 0
65	  },
66	  "alwaysContext": [
67	    {
68	      "id": "project",
69	      "path": ".agent-context/project.md",
70	      "description": "Stable project brief",
71	      "sha256": "...",
72	      "content": "# Project brief\n..."
73	    }
74	  ],
75	  "onDemandCatalog": [
76	    {
77	      "id": "architecture",
78	      "path": ".agent-context/architecture.md",
79	      "description": "System boundaries",
80	      "sha256": "...",
81	      "triggers": ["architecture changes"]
82	    }
83	  ],
84	  "diagnostics": []
85	}
86	```
87	
88	The real envelope includes all six required checkpoint sections and the configured context catalog;
89	digests are omitted above only to keep the example readable.
90	
91	## How it works
92	
93	```text
94	.agent-context/ (canonical, human-reviewable memory)
95	                         |
96	                         v
97	              deterministic compiler
98	                         |
99	              +----------+----------+----------+
100	              |          |          |          |
101	           AGENTS.md  CLAUDE.md  GEMINI.md   Skills
102	              |          |          |          |
103	        Codex/Cursor  Claude Code  Gemini CLI  continuity
104	```
105	
106	The adapters are small routers. Stable purpose, architecture, current state, decisions, and handoff
107	remain reviewable Markdown sources in `.agent-context/`. Generated blocks preserve surrounding human
108	instructions and fail closed on ownership conflicts.
109	
110	## Install the published beta
111	
112	Node.js 22 or newer and a Git worktree are required.
113	
114	For one-off evaluation of the current published beta:
115	
116	```bash
117	npx --yes carrylog@beta init
118	npx --yes carrylog@beta validate
119	```
120	
121	For a persistent global CLI:
122	
123	```bash
124	npm install --global carrylog@beta
125	carrylog init
126	carrylog validate
127	```
128	
129	For a team-pinned development dependency:
130	
131	```bash
132	npm install --save-dev --save-exact carrylog@0.1.0-beta.5
133	npx --no-install carrylog init
134	npx --no-install carrylog validate
135	```
136	
137	Beta.5 provides the reviewed universal Codex/Claude/Cursor/Gemini surfaces and portable
138	`checkpoint`/`resume` workflow. Pin the exact version when reproducible team installations matter.
139	
140	## Build from source
141	
142	Node.js 22 or newer and a Git worktree are required.
143	
144	```bash
145	git clone https://github.com/Jaemani/Carrylog.git
146	cd Carrylog
147	npm ci
148	npm run build
149	
150	# Run against another repository without a global installation.
151	node /path/to/Carrylog/dist/cli.js init --root /path/to/your-project
152	node /path/to/Carrylog/dist/cli.js validate --root /path/to/your-project
153	```
154	
155	After an agent finishes meaningful work:
156	
157	```bash
158	node /path/to/Carrylog/dist/cli.js checkpoint --root /path/to/your-project
159	```
160	
161	Then inspect the same verified state before continuing with another harness:
162	
163	```bash
164	node /path/to/Carrylog/dist/cli.js resume --check --json --root /path/to/your-project
165	```
166	
167	`init` creates the canonical context, Codex/Cursor `AGENTS.md`, Claude `CLAUDE.md`, Gemini
168	`GEMINI.md`, and continuity Skills. Carrylog does not contact a model, upload context, stage, commit,
169	or push.
170	
171	Do not mix one-off initialization with a later bare `carrylog` command. Bare commands require a
172	global installation or a package script that exposes local `.bin`; use `npx --no-install carrylog`
173	for a project dependency. One-off initialization does not leave an executable for later automated
174	resume. Generated Skills never download or upgrade Carrylog implicitly.
175	
176	### Migrating from `@jaemani/agent-context-kit@0.1.0-beta.3`
177	
178	Carrylog preserves the configuration v1 root, schema, and managed markers published by
179	`@jaemani/agent-context-kit@0.1.0-beta.3`. Existing
180	repositories do not move or duplicate `.agent-context/`; only generated adapter prose and commands
181	change after synchronization. `carrylog sync` also recognizes that package's complete untouched
182	instructions template at any configured document path and changes only its executable name, including
183	its CRLF form. If customized always-loaded context still contains a command-shaped `ackit` invocation,
184	Carrylog reports `E_LEGACY_CLI_INSTRUCTION` and requires review instead of rewriting it speculatively.
185	Historical prose that only names the old command is not treated as an invocation.
186	
187	For a global installation:
188	
189	```bash
190	npm uninstall --global @jaemani/agent-context-kit
191	npm install --global carrylog@beta
192	carrylog sync
193	carrylog validate
194	```
195	
196	For a project dependency:
197	
198	```bash
199	npm uninstall @jaemani/agent-context-kit
200	npm install --save-dev --save-exact carrylog@0.1.0-beta.5
201	npx --no-install carrylog sync
202	npx --no-install carrylog validate
203	```
204	
205	Also update package scripts, CI commands, and JavaScript/TypeScript import specifiers that name the old
206	package or executable. Carrylog intentionally does not install the old `ackit` binary or the
207	Windows-conflicting `cl` alias.
208	
209	## Commands

212	
213	Creates configuration v2, canonical context documents, the matching copied schema, managed
214	Codex/Cursor, Claude Code, and Gemini CLI routers, and continuity Skills by default.
215	
216	```bash
217	carrylog init --name "Example project"
218	carrylog init --adapters codex,claude,cursor,gemini
219	carrylog init --dry-run
220	carrylog init --adopt
